prompt:
Image 1 is a reference sheet of one specific person. Image 2 is a club crest. Image 3 is a flat lay of the exact kit they wear — shirt, shorts, socks, footwear and ball.

Photograph THAT EXACT PERSON — same face, same bone structure, same hair, same build,
same age — playing Swimming.

HAIR — this is identity, not styling, and it does not change between frames:
VERY PALE PLATINUM BLONDE hair, fine, straight and flyaway, with no fringe. In every photograph it is pulled BACK off the face and gathered at the back of the head, with fine loose strands escaping around the hairline and temples — photo4.png shows them lifting in the wind. Its full LENGTH is not visible in any photograph, because it is tied back in all four and under a cap in two; the DECISION is that it falls to just below the shoulders when it is down, fine and straight, the ends a little lighter and dry from chlorine. The SWIM CAP is not hair and is not part of this line — it is a kit item, worn only to swim.
It is exactly as in the reference sheet. Do not restyle it, do not change the number of
braids or plaits, do not tie it differently, do not tuck it away, do not add or remove a
fringe. If the pose would move it, it moves the way that hair moves — it does not become
different hair.

BUILD — this is the person's actual body and it does not change between frames:
A SIXTEEN-YEAR-OLD SWIMMER'S body as photo2.png shows it, and it is a teenage girl's: tall and LEAN with long arms and long legs, the shoulders broader than the hips but only moderately so — a soft V rather than a heavy one — a long flat midsection, narrow hips and smooth, lightly defined limbs with no bulk anywhere. Reproduce this body as it is: do NOT give her a powerlifter's shoulders or a grown woman's figure, and do NOT slim her.
Reproduce it exactly. Do NOT slim them down, do NOT make them heavier, do NOT add muscle
definition they do not have or take away what they do. An athletic photograph is not a
licence to redraw somebody's body — this is a real person and the picture is for them.

POSE: standing at her full height on the pool deck, caught at the end of a shoulder swing: both arms just swept back and down with the chest open and the shoulder blades together, up on the balls of both feet, water still running off her shoulders and forearms, chin down, eyes lifted into the lens under the brow. Stopped between two movements, not posed.
CAMERA: eye level, straight on with the body turned a few degrees, 85 mm lens at f/2.8, full body.
FACING: square to the camera; she sits in the CENTRE of the composite, so she leans neither left nor right — the swimmer's V of her back and shoulders is what the frame is for.
EQUIPMENT: the royal blue silicone SWIM CAP is on with all of her hair under it, and the GOGGLES are PUSHED UP onto the forehead above the eyebrows so the whole face is clear and readable. BARE FEET — no shoes anywhere in the frame. NOTHING in her hands and no block, no lane rope, no kickboard and no water in the frame.

UNIFORM AND EQUIPMENT — every item comes from image 3, exactly as shown there. The shirt, the shorts, the socks, the boots and the ball are THOSE items: same colours, same design, same shape, same condition — clean and unmarked. This includes the CUT, and the SLEEVE LENGTH above all: if the shirt in image 3 has long sleeves, this athlete wears long sleeves, and if they are pushed up to the elbows they are pushed up here too. Long sleeves in one frame and short in another is the same athlete in two different shirts. Also match the collar and any piping exactly. Do not substitute a different boot, do not change the sock colour, do not swap the ball. Image 3 is the complete wardrobe for this athlete and there is nothing left to decide.
Primary colour #1F4EA1, secondary #FFFFFF.

SLEEVES: copy the garment in the kit image. If it has short sleeves this athlete
wears short sleeves and it is NOT a sleeveless vest; if it is sleeveless, so is this.
GRAPHICS: the badge is the ONLY mark on the shirt besides the number. No
manufacturer's logo, no second badge, no lettering of any kind anywhere on the kit.

THE KIT — these are settled decisions, not suggestions. Do not substitute anything.
- shirt: A ROYAL BLUE ONE-PIECE COMPETITION SWIMSUIT exactly as photo2.png shows it, and it is the WHOLE uniform — one single garment covering the torso and fastening between the legs. A plain round SCOOP NECKLINE, narrow shoulder straps that run over the shoulder and join into a RACERBACK behind (the straps meet in a single panel between the shoulder blades — this is a racing suit, not a strappy one), and legs cut HIGH at the hip. The body of it is PLAIN ROYAL BLUE all over: there is NO contrasting stripe down the sides, no panel and no trim of any other colour, whatever the sport default says. The club badge sits CENTRED ON THE CHEST, printed in WHITE — the bayline-marlins mark with its ARCH outline (flat base, semicircular top) drawn as a narrow band with the marlin inside it, about a palm across. It is the ONLY mark on the suit. NO maker's logo, NO club name, NO player name, NO number and no lettering anywhere. The BACK of the suit is not visible in any photograph; the DECISION is that it is a PLAIN CLOSED BACK in the same royal blue — no number, no name, no badge and no lettering across the shoulders or anywhere on it. Swimming does not number a racing suit, and a number printed across her back would be a mark this suit does not have.
- shorts: There is NO separate lower garment of any kind: no shorts, no jammers, no tights, no briefs under the suit. The one-piece racing suit IS the whole uniform, and her LEGS ARE BARE from the high-cut hip to the floor, exactly as photo2.png shows her on the pool deck.
- socks: NO SOCKS. Swimming is competed barefoot and no sock appears in any photograph. Her feet and ankles are bare in every frame.
- footwear: BARE FEET. No shoes, no sandals, no pool slides of any kind — she stands and walks on the wet deck barefoot, exactly as photo2.png shows. Do not put footwear on her in any frame.
- equipment: TWO ITEMS BELONG TO THE KIT, and they are worn to SWIM rather than all day: a plain ROYAL BLUE SILICONE SWIM CAP, smooth and completely unmarked — no maker's logo, no lettering, no club name — covering the whole head with the hairline showing at the front, and GOGGLES with dark MIRRORED lenses in a soft silver-grey on plain dark straps, also unbranded. photo2.png shows both at the pool, the goggles hanging around her NECK, which is where they sit when she is not actually swimming; photo3.png shows the goggles on at the wall. In photo1.png and photo4.png, away from the pool, she wears neither — they are kit, not part of her. She also carries a plain unbranded MESH KIT BAG on one shoulder in photo2.png, on the way out. The DECISION for the poses is that the cap and goggles are ON in every frame and the bag is NOT: no kit bag, no kickboard, no float, no paddles and no towel in her hands.
- Where an item above is described from the athlete's own photographs, any manufacturer's
  logo it genuinely carries stays on it — that is their real clothing.
- The club crest sits CENTRED ON THE CHEST of the swimsuit, about a palm across, as photo2.png shows it. That position is a settled decision, not a convention to be corrected: do not move it to the left chest, do not shrink it and do not add a second mark beside it. That position is settled and is the same in every frame.
THE BADGE: take the artwork in image 2 and apply it to the shirt UNCHANGED — a finished
graphic being printed onto a garment, not a subject to redraw. Identical outline, identical
figure, identical colours in identical places, identical proportions, and its white stays
WHITE and fully opaque against the shirt — never tinted, faded or blended into the fabric
colour. It creases and shades with the cloth, but the artwork itself does not change.
SIZE: about a hand's width at this scale. It is the ONLY badge on the kit.
PLACEMENT: the badge sits CENTRED ON THE CHEST of the swimsuit, about a palm across, as photo2.png shows it. That position is a settled decision, not a convention to be corrected: do not move it to the left chest, do not shrink it and do not add a second mark beside it. Exactly there, at that scale, in every frame. It is a settled decision, not a convention to be corrected: do not move it, do not enlarge it, do not let it dominate the shirt.
Any number on the front of the shirt is the one in image 3, in the same place and the same colours. No other number, and no lettering of any kind.

This must look like an actual photograph of an actual person, taken by a person with a
camera. Skin has visible texture and slightly uneven tone, with a light natural warmth
where they have been working — and NEVER a deep red, blotchy or overheated-looking face:
no scarlet cheeks, no burning nose, no sunburnt flush. The resting colour of their skin
is the colour of their skin. Hair is made of separate strands with flyaways, not a moulded mass. Eyebrows are
uneven. The face is asymmetric, the way every real face is. Fabric creases and bunches at
the joints where the body moves.
A TEENAGER, not an adult: the jaw and neck are not fully filled out, and the skin shows
it — fine texture and slightly uneven tone, at most one or two faint blemishes near the
hairline, and uneven patchy stubble at most on a boy. NOT a breakout: no cluster of
spots, nothing raised, nothing angry or red across the cheeks, nose or chin.

CONDITION — this is a premium shot and everything worn or held is CLEAN:
- The kit is clean and in good condition: no mud, no grass stains, no dirt patches, no
  sweat marks on the fabric, no tears, no fading, no visible wear.
- Footwear is clean: no caked mud, no scuffing, no dirt on the soles or laces.
- Any ball or equipment is clean: no dirt, no scuffs, no staining.
- The ATHLETE may look like they have been playing — a LIGHT natural warmth in the face,
  damp hair, a little real sweat at the temples and neck. That belongs to the person, never
  to the kit. Do NOT make the face deep red or blotchy: a hot, over-red face is the single
  most common way these frames stop looking premium.
- FOOTWEAR AND EQUIPMENT ARE THE SAME OBJECTS IN EVERY POSE: identical boots or shoes in
  the same colour and condition, and the same ball or implement. Three of these frames are
  composited side by side on one card, so a change of boot between them reads as an error.

Lighting, identical in every shot: ONE dominant directional source from camera-left and
above, hard enough to cast shadows with edges — like daylight through the high windows of
a sports hall. The shadow side of the face is left mostly UNFILLED, so there is real
contrast across it. One weak bounce from the right, nothing else.
Slightly cool and slightly uneven, not perfectly neutral.
This is NOT a beauty or commercial lighting setup: no big soft wraparound key, no glamour
rim light tracing the whole silhouette, no even fill flattening the face, no colour gels,
no atmosphere, no haze, no lens flare.

Hard requirements — this image will be cut out and composited, so:
- Flat, evenly lit seamless mid-grey (18% grey) studio backdrop, completely plain — no gradient, no vignette, no floor line, no shadow on it, no set.
- The athlete is ALONE and stands on nothing: no ground, no floor, no field, no court,
  no arena, no crowd, no other people, no spray, no particles, no smoke.
- FRAMING: leave a clear empty band of backdrop around the athlete on ALL FOUR sides,
  roughly a hand's width at this scale. Nothing may touch or cross a frame edge — not
  the top of the head, not a foot, and above all not the far end of any equipment, which
  is the thing that gets clipped. If the pose does not fit, PULL THE CAMERA BACK. Never
  change the pose to make it fit and never let anything run off the edge.
- the whole athlete head to bare feet, the face sharp and lit with the goggles clear of the eyes, the cap on and the shoulders wet, both hands open and visible, nothing cropped.
- HANDS: both hands are drawn anatomically, in full, and they read as hands. FIVE fingers
  on each, separated from one another with visible gaps and daylight between them where
  they are apart — never fused into a mitten, never melting into each other, never a
  smooth paddle of skin, and never more or fewer than five. Each hand does something a
  real athlete's hand does in this movement: gripping, open and flat, reaching, or hanging
  loose — and both hands agree with the effort in the rest of the body. Where the hands
  are near each other they may TOUCH, but each one stays a separate readable hand with its
  own outline. Wrists bend the way wrists bend.
- Vertical 2:3, the athlete filling most of the height.
- FIT: the kit HANGS on them. The shirt drapes from the shoulders with room through the chest and body and does not cling to the stomach or the ribs; the sleeves are loose on the arms; the shorts hang rather than grip. Loose the way a real team kit is, NOT tight and NOT sagging or oversized — the fit shown on the flat lay, worn.
- BRANDING: whatever image 3 shows is right. If an item there carries a manufacturer's mark, keep it exactly; if it is plain, it stays plain. Never add a swoosh, three stripes, a cat, a jumpman or a trefoil that image 3 does not have.
- Sharp throughout. No motion blur, no shallow-focus blur. Keep any contact shadow tight
  under the feet — no long cast shadow across the backdrop, no floor-to-wall seam.
- No text, no lettering, no sponsor marks, no brand logos, no watermark — the chest crest is the only exception.
NO REAL-WORLD LEAGUE OR CLUB MARKS, ANYWHERE, EVER. No NFL shield, no NBA, no MLB, no NHL,
no FIFA, no UEFA, no Premier League, no NCAA, no Olympic rings, no national federation
badge, no professional club's crest — not on a jersey, a helmet, a sleeve, a collar, a
label, a ball or a boot, not even small and not even partly hidden. The only badge that
may appear anywhere is the club crest supplied with this request. These emblems carry no
letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
Any lettering that legitimately appears — a maker's wordmark on a glove, a skate or a
helmet — reads FORWARDS and the right way up, exactly as it does on the real item. Never
mirrored, never reversed, never upside down, never scrambled, even on a limb turned away
from the camera. Reversed lettering is a generation artefact, not a photograph.
- No airbrushed, retouched or beauty-filtered skin. No skin smoothing of any kind.
- No waxy or plastic sheen on the face, no glowing translucent skin, no mannequin look.
- No 3D render, no CGI, no video-game character, no digital sculpt, no illustration.
- No perfectly symmetric face, no flawless white teeth, no poreless skin.
- No stock-photo or catalogue look. This is a photograph of one specific person, not a model.
